concept.subject: A planted field at the edge of a wood, its rows of low leafy plants and sandy furrows running from the horizon toward the viewer.
concept.composition: The treeline and a strip of sky fill the top third, the field's far edge crosses at a third of the height, and the furrows fan out from a point under the cannon to the lower corners; the field fills everything below.
concept.layout: Round pegs only, 158 of them. The plants are a plinko grid: a staggered lattice fill over the whole field. Peg lines run down the four furrows that fan out from the horizon, the two near ones to the bottom and the two far ones to the walls, and along the field's far edge beside the cannon; the lattice keeps its clearance from them, so the furrows read as lanes. Two short rails lie in the field just below its far edge, left and right, sloping toward the middle and sheltering the rows under them, and a round stone sits where the near furrows meet under the cannon.

difficulty.note: The stage's easiest level: an open grid where most drops light several pegs, a gentle step from stage 1's counts up to stage 2's.

background.prompt: A photo of a planted field in late summer, low leafy plants in rows on light sandy soil. A pale sky fills the top tenth, a dark treeline crosses from about a tenth to a quarter of the picture height, rising a little to the right, and the field's far edge runs straight across at about 27 percent of the height. Sandy furrows fan out from a point just left of the center on that edge: the two near ones run to about a quarter and two thirds of the width at the bottom, the far ones to the left edge at about three fifths of the height and to the right edge at about 70 percent. Between them, rows of green plants fill the field to the bottom.

picture.title: A sprawling peanut field in rural North Carolina, showcasing rows of mature peanut plants ready for harvest.
picture.author: Mark Stebnicki
